# 1933 Double Eagle

The 1933 double eagle is a $20 gold coin of the Saint-Gaudens design,
and the most famous rarity in American numismatics. The mintage was
445,500 pieces, but the 1933 gold recall meant virtually the entire
issue was melted before release; none were ever officially issued for
circulation.

A small number escaped the melt. For decades the Secret Service
confiscated every example that surfaced, and only one — the Weitzman
specimen, with its export licence — is legal for private ownership.

In June 2021 the Weitzman specimen sold at Sotheby's for $18.9 million,
making the 1933 double eagle the most expensive coin ever sold at
auction.

See [[Mint Records]] for production ledgers and
[[Most Expensive Coins]] for the auction record list.
